title: Scraper: Extend MSI to Threadripper / Threadripper Pro
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Extend the existing MsiScraper to cover sTRX4, sTR5, and possibly sWRX8 MSI Creator-line boards.

board_class: Threadripper, ThreadripperPro (limited — MSI's WRX80 catalog is small).

MSI boards in scope:
- sTRX4: Creator TRX40, TRX40 PRO WIFI
- sTR5: Creator TRX50 (forthcoming)
- sWRX8: MSI does not currently ship a WRX80 board, skip unless one appears

Implementation:
- src/psp_etl/scrape/msi.py uses Wayback CDX against download.msi.com/bos_exe/mb/* — no socket filter at the URL level, every board ID is enumerated.
- The socket filter is in `_AM4_RE` / `_AM5_RE` chipset regexes inside `_identify_board`. Boards not matching either are dropped (`return None`).
- Add a `_TR_RE` for TRX40 / TRX50 chipset tokens and a `_TR_PRO_RE` for WRX80, then return the matching socket name.
- `classify_board_class` in ingest.py already maps sTRX4/sTR5/sWRX8 → Threadripper/ThreadripperPro.

This is the **simplest** of the four extension issues — MSI's range-request board-identification approach already enumerates every board on the CDN, so the change is just regex updates plus a socket-name decision (TRX40 → sTRX4, TRX50 → sTR5).

Acceptance criteria:
- Existing AM4/AM5 tests pass
- New tests for one TRX40 board enumerate via CDX and return socket=sTRX4
- Updated regexes documented in code comments

Related: #79, #81.
